set.approach: Park at the Mirror Lake picnic ground off Wyoming 130, the Snowy Range Road, a seasonal road. The route climbs the Sundial Slab, which you reach by scrambling north from the picnic ground. The start is below a V-shaped chimney.

review.notes: Route page states Mirror Lake picnic ground and a scramble north to Sundial Slab, and the V-shaped chimney start. Descent not stated, so omitted.

set.descent_text: From the top, descend the lower-angle couloir on the north side of Old Main. The route faces the sun and sits under a big funnel, so avoid it when there is much snow on the slopes above.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent couloir north of Old Main and the avalanche funnel. Approach not stated, omitted.

set.descent_text: The couloir ends near the Medicine Bow Peak summit ridge. Turn north, tag the summit, and follow the trail back down to the Lakes Trail. Turning south and following the Medicine Bow trail down to Lake Marie is longer. The couloir faces due east, so start early.
set.approach: From the Mirror Lake trailhead, follow the Lakes Trail until you are just north of Lookout Lake. Leave the trail, scramble and bushwhack to the northern edge of Old Main, then traverse north to the base of the couloir. It is shaped like a goose bending its head around a rock near the top.

review.notes: Both from the Gooseneck route page; the summit-trail and east-facing fact also consistent with the area page. Single route page, hence medium.

set.approach: Start at the west Lake Marie trailhead and follow the fishing path to the north end of Lake Marie. Climb the scree to the obvious dihedral between the Diamond Buttress and the Diamond, where the gully starts. It is best in fall and early winter, before the Snowy Range Road closes for the season.

review.notes: Route page for approach and season; descent not stated.

set.approach: Start at the Lake Marie recreation area beside Wyoming 130, the Snowy Range Road, which is a seasonal road. A faint path leaves the picnic ground and runs to the foot of the scree, then you choose your own line over the talus to the cliff. Snow and ice often linger at the base into early summer, so an ice axe and crampons are useful in early season. The route is the roof at the far right end of the Little Diamond, the first line right of Guillotine.

review.notes: Approach from the area page (Lake Marie recreation area, faint trail to scree, cross-country); early-season axe/crampons from both pages.

set.descent_text: The route finishes about 30 feet below the summit, and easy scrambling takes you to the top. From the top, walk south across easy ground to the Medicine Bow Peak trail and follow it down to the Lake Marie parking area. Loose rock is everywhere on this face, so move carefully.

set.descent_text: The route finishes close to the Medicine Bow Peak trail, so hikers may be watching your last pitch. Turn left, south and west, onto the trail and follow it down to the Lake Marie parking area.
set.approach: The route is on the Schoolhouse, the formation directly above the Lake Marie parking lot. Follow the scree field up from the parking lot to the base. The line is the clean right-facing corner low on the face, about the middle of the cliff.

review.notes: Single route page covers both; trail location consistent with area page. Rappel option on the page omitted, unconfirmed.

set.descent_text: The trail is about 20 feet past the top of the couloir. Turn left onto the Medicine Bow Peak trail to return to the parking lot, or go right to continue to the summit. In good snow you can also ski or glissade the couloir.
set.approach: Park at the Lake Marie lot beside Wyoming 130, a seasonal road, and follow the sidewalk to the lake. Break left and go around the lake to the foot of the couloirs, scramble up a few boulders, and the couloir starts under the Diamond Buttress and runs left of it.

review.notes: Route page; area page and lake-trail context agree on starting at Lake Marie.

set.approach: The shortest way in is from the Medicine Bow Peak trail, but a more scenic line starts from Lake Marie and goes to Lookout Lake. From Lookout Lake you climb a slope of your choice to the ridge. Bearing left gives steeper ground, and heading straight north is milder. An ice axe and crampons or traction devices are useful.

review.notes: Route page only; descent not stated.
